interpretation: Post-hoc same-seed counterfactual diagnosis, not independent policy confirmation. Fork a recorded world before a decision and force the first target-agent speed choice by its exploration RNG. Restore the same future target decision RNG after that first choice in both forks; other initial RNG streams remain identical. Later dynamics and population can diverge. Normal learning continues in each diagnostic fork. No fork outcome enters the baseline or trains a live agent. Compare short and longer target-agent energy effects; limited-horizon effects do not establish optimal long-run actions.
